issues.detail: The Hebrew first-person singular verbs (תָמוּתִי 'I die', אָמוּת 'I will die', אֶקָּבֵר 'I will be buried') are rendered as third-person 'con' (you) throughout, reversing the speaker. The Hebrew speaker is Ruth speaking about herself; the Vietnamese makes the speaker address 'con' as the subject.

The Hebrew 'בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵךְ' means 'between me and you' (first person + second person feminine singular). The Vietnamese 'con khỏi nàng' means 'you from her' (second person + third person), changing the person of the second party from 'you' to 'her'.
